title: fix(driver-sql): emit large $or / $and groups as balanced halves so gated comment and attachment reads fit hosted libSQL's depth limit
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-zhuang"} -->
_Requested by **Sam** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01GsBogozeZG5sdpAARrN7HP?thread=cmsg_01GsBogozeZG5sdpAARrN7HPPVFZSDfCpi1vgzUi5CzyLT)_

Part of #29888. The card carries no `Claim:` naming this branch, so the closing-target guard refuses a closing keyword on this pull; the dispatching seat finishes the card after this lands.

## What changes

- `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-balanced-group.ts` (new): `emitBalancedGroup` emits the members of a `$and` / `$or` group. A group of at most 8 members is emitted flat, byte-identical to before. A larger group is split into two parenthesised halves, recursively, until each part has at most 8 members.
- `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts`: the `$and` and `$or` arms of `applyFilterCondition` (the only place either combinator is emitted) go through `emitBalancedGroup`. `driver-turso` and `driver-sqlite-wasm` extend `SqlDriver`, so they inherit it.
- Tests: `sql-driver-balanced-group.test.ts` (driver unit) and `comment-attachment-gate-expression-depth.dogfood.test.ts` (the card's reads at the HTTP door).
- Changeset: `@objectstack/driver-sql` patch.

## Why

SQL `OR` / `AND` are binary and left-associative, so the flat `(b1) or (b2) or … or (bN)` the compiler wrote parses into a tree N levels deep. The comment-thread gate (plugin-audit) and the attachment gate (service-storage) OR one `ReadableIds` branch per registered parent object, so N grows with the deployment: a bare environment registers about 80. A hosted libSQL server refuses a tree deeper than 100 (`Expression tree is too large (maximum depth 100)`), so every gated read answered 500 `DATABASE_ERROR` on hosted environments. Local SQLite allows 1000, which is why a local stack answered 200.

The fix goes in the driver, where the tree is compiled, rather than in the gates. The `$or` in the filter AST has no depth, and only the SQL text decides how the database nests it. Balancing at compile time fixes both gates and any other large group, and the gates' WHERE stays the same. AND and OR are associative and commutative under SQL's three-valued logic, so the regrouped expression selects the same rows on every dialect. A group of N members now adds at most `7 + ceil(log2(N / 8))` levels: 11 for 130 branches, 14 for 1,200.

The card's other option, narrowing on `thread_id` / `parent_object` the way #24177 does, would shorten the chain only for reads that name their parent. An unfiltered or sorted read would still carry every branch, so this PR does not take that route.

## Verification

The repo's test SQLite builds (better-sqlite3, sql.js) allow 1000 levels and expose no `sqlite3_limit`. Both tests measure a 100-level budget the way SQLite counts it. The statement the driver compiled runs with its WHERE as the left operand of 900 `and 1` terms, so it fits under 1000 exactly when the WHERE alone fits under 100. Each test proves this calibration before it measures anything:
- Driver unit: a 99-term flat OR chain is accepted under the budget and a 100-term chain is refused.
- Dogfood: a 90-level WHERE is served, a 110-level WHERE is refused with SQLite's own message, and the same 110-level WHERE is served with the budget off. This runs through the real driver path as an `assertArmed` control.

| Test | Before the fix | After the fix |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `sql-driver-balanced-group.test.ts` (7 cases: `$or` of 9 / 130 / 1,200 branches, `$and` of 130, nesting under `$not`, the flat ≤ 8 form) | 3 failed (130 and 1,200 `$or`, 130 `$and`) | 7 passed |
| `comment-attachment-gate-expression-depth.dogfood.test.ts` (8 cases, 130 extra parent objects) | 8 failed, every read **500** under the budget | 8 passed |

The dogfood cases are the card's own query strings, sent as the member at the HTTP door with the real `SecurityPlugin`, `AuditPlugin`, `StorageServicePlugin` and the sql.js driver: `sys_comment?top=…&sort=created_at`, `sys_comment?filter=["thread_id","=",…]`, and `sys_attachment?filter=["and",["parent_object","=",…],["parent_id","=",…]]`. Each case is asserted with the budget on and off, and both answers must have the same status, rows and `total`. The test also checks that withheld rows stay withheld: a comment or attachment on the writer's private case, or on an object the member may not read, is not served by list, total or filter. The writer's and the administrator's reads are served under the budget too.

The before column was measured by restoring `sql-driver.ts` from `main` and rebuilding `driver-sql` (dogfood resolves the built output), with the tests unchanged. Readings were taken on this branch at its head.

Package suites run on this branch (before the `main` merge; the scoped re-check after it is green): driver-sql 3858 passed, driver-turso 2496, driver-sqlite-wasm 750, plugin-audit 1120, service-storage 1326, 0 failures. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-sql typecheck` is clean, eslint on the changed files is clean, and 63 of the 66 gates `dispatch-gates` derives pass. The other 3 are prerequisites of this container (a shallow clone, a no-DTS build, unbuilt packages) and say nothing about this diff.

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

The diff changes no contract or schema. The SQL text changes only for groups of more than 8 members, and their answers stay the same.

### Acceptance notes

- `service-analytics`' native SQL compiler (`read-scope-sql.ts`) joins a `$or` / `$and` the same flat way. It compiles RLS read scopes for analytics queries, not these gates, and nothing measured here reaches it at depth. It is noted here, not changed.
- The order also named `parent-record-read-gate.ts` and the `ReadableIds` path. Neither needed a change: their WHERE is correct, and only its SQL nesting was too deep.
